one_month_reasoning: Eaton's own Q3 2026 report is estimated for about Nov 3, 2026 (after the Oct 30 window), so no company earnings print falls inside the month. What does fall inside is the late-October peer and hyperscaler reporting season (GE Vernova, Vertiv, then Microsoft/Alphabet/Meta/Amazon capex commentary in the last week of October). Those are two-sided: Alphabet has already flagged a 'significant increase' in 2027 capex (supportive), but the Sept 14 episode (-7.6% on an AI-pace debate plus a GLJ Sell on GEV) shows the name reacts sharply to any capex-pacing hint. The stock has already rebounded from ~$395 to $432, so I apply no momentum or reversal tilt. Distribution: median ~$434 (tiny drift), sigma ~11.5% for the month (39%/3.5 = 11.1%, nudged up for the hyperscaler capex prints), roughly symmetric in log space.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (60%): Sep-2027 NTM EPS ~$17.4 x 26x = $452, and EV/sales (40%): NTM sales ~$39.9B x 4.7x less ~$18B net debt over 389.5M shares = $436. Blended fair value ~$446, a bit above today's $432.

inputs_detail.derivation: 2027E x ~1.14. That is below the 2026-to-2027 consensus step of about 17%, because hyperscaler capex growth is forecast to decelerate sharply by 2028 (Morgan Stanley: 93% to 61% to 14%). It is still backed by an Americas backlog up 33% and Global up 103%.

Today ~27.4x 2027E ($432/$15.75). I take off ~1.5 turns because the AI-power group de-rated on the Sept 14 episode and growth decelerates into 2028. The multiple stays above the industrial average because of a backlog lasting several years.

methods.inputs: NTM sales Sep 2027 ~$39.9B x 4.7x = EV $187.5B; net debt ~$18B; 389.5M shares

Current EV ~$188B ($432.28 x 389.5M + $19.9B net debt) / 2027E sales $36.63B = 5.1x. I compress this ~8% for decelerating growth.
Q2 debt $20.6B less $0.695B cash. Paydown from FCF (Q2 FCF $874M/quarter) is partly offset by the EUR 810M COL Group purchase, dividends and buybacks.

bear.story: Hyperscalers signal 2027-28 capex digestion or a slower AI build (the Sept 14 fear becomes real), and data center orders roll over from +240%/+65% comps. 2028 EPS gets cut toward $16 and the multiple de-rates to ~20x NTM, as in the GLJ 'cyclical priced as secular' critique.

base.story: Guidance is met ($13.50 in 2026, ~$15.75 in 2027) and the data center backlog converts. Bellevue switchgear and new European capacity ramp in 2027. The multiple compresses modestly to ~26x on NTM EPS of about $17.4.

bull.story: 2027 capex rises significantly (per Alphabet), Boyd liquid cooling and 800V DC/SST orders land in 2H26-2027, and EPS revisions run toward $16.5 for 2027 and $19+ for 2028. The stock re-rates to about 31-32x as a grid-to-chip platform.

thesis_break_reason: Near the Street low target ($333) and ~24% below today, under the Sept low (~$390) and the 2026 lows. A trade there within the year most likely means data center orders turned negative or 2027 guidance came in well below the ~$15.75 consensus, i.e. the AI-capex cycle is rolling over and this is not ordinary volatility (monthly sigma is ~11%).

reasoning: Fundamentals come from the Q2 2026 8-K: record $8.5B sales (+14% organic), adj EPS $3.15, FY guide raised to $13.40-13.60, Americas orders +41% and backlog +33%, Global backlog +103%. Street 2027 EPS is ~$15.75. At $432 the stock trades ~27x 2027E. My lane sources were alt/independent: a Substack view that Eaton is racing Schneider on integration, a September hyperscaler capex newsletter, trade press on Boyd and 800V DC, and job-posting and plant-expansion data (Bellevue switchgear plant, 200+ hires, NC hiring). They say demand and capacity are still expanding, and 2026 capex guides were raised across the board. The Sept 14 selloff (verified by two sources: 24/7 Wall St and TradingKey) shows the main risk is the multiple, not near-term earnings. Reddit was blocked from fetching, and I found no relevant prediction market, so research was limited. Fair value is ~$446 (P/E and EV/sales blend), only slightly above spot. Scenario mean is ~$452 (0.22 x 305 + 0.53 x 455 + 0.25 x 590). I centred a lognormal on ~$445 with sigma ~0.34, a bit below the 39% realized vol because realized was inflated by the September shock. I then fattened the left tail slightly for capex-digestion risk. The result is P(>=432) ~0.53, P(>=346) ~0.77 and P(>=584) ~0.21.
